tagline: A pixel-art status strip for Claude Code, and a three-minute look at how a mod draws it.
about: What each tile on the strip means, the walker's five moods, sections and 12 palettes, then how a mod works: hooks, events, state, and the cell grid that becomes the strip.
note: Needs a Claude Code build with the mods API (tested on 2.1.308). The strip appears under the prompt right away.

tagline: Every Claude turn committed to a shadow git repo you can browse and restore from.
about: How each turn becomes a commit in a shadow repo next to your project's own .git, how to opt a project in, the two shell hooks that do the work, what a commit holds, and how to look back and restore a file.
note: Opt in per project with /history:enable. Needs git and python3.

tagline: Author, run and sandbox dev containers from Claude Code.
about: Writing a devcontainer.json from slash commands, running the container, sandbox mode (Claude's Bash calls rewritten to run inside the container by a PreToolUse hook), auto-rebuild on config edits, and what stays off until you turn it on.
note: Needs Docker for up, build and exec, and Node.js for the devcontainers CLI. Hooks stay off until you enable them.

tagline: Turn a code change into an interactive lesson.
about: What you can point /explain:diff at, what it reads before writing a word, the sections of the lesson it produces (diagrams, walkthrough, trade-offs, a scored quiz), and why it is a skill rather than a hook.
note: Reads the repository and runs read-only git commands. Writes one HTML file under /tmp.
